prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
The blog is built, published and rendering. Umbraco is still running, so you can open it right away.

**What I built, all schema and content through the MCP server**
- Five block element types in the Blocks folder: hero, rich text, image with caption, pull quote, and a post list that reads the child posts of the current page.
- One custom Block Grid data type "Page Blocks" holding those five blocks. The save handler filed it under Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid as rule 3 requires.
- Two page types in the Pages folder, Blog Home and Blog Post, each with a block grid property, with templates attached and Site Root updated to allow Blog Home beneath it.
- A Blog media folder with six Unsplash photos imported from the local folder. Captions credit the photographers.
- A "Blog" home node under WWW with domain `/`, plus two published posts: "One protocol, every tool: why MCP is the USB-C of AI" and "This blog built itself". Each post is a block grid of rich text, images and a quote.

**Razor layer, written after the stop, build and restart**
- Plain block models in `Models/Blocks/`, one ViewComponent per block in `ViewComponents/`, and markup only in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`.
- Adapter partials in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` that map the block item to the plain model and invoke the component. Pages render with Umbraco's own block grid helper. No custom loops or wrappers.
- A shared layout, the two page templates, and block grid plus rich text styles appended to the Tailwind source, built into `wwwroot/dist`.

**How to view it**

```
https://localhost:44317/
https://localhost:44317/one-protocol-every-tool/
https://localhost:44317/this-blog-built-itself/
```

Backoffice is at `/umbraco` with admin@example.com and password 1234567890.

**Verified**
- All three URLs return 200 with no "Could not render component" fallbacks. Signed crop URLs and the CSS load. Screenshots of the home and a post page looked right.
- uSync exported every new content type, data type, template, media item and content node.

**Things to know**
- My first boot bypassed the launch profile, so the site started without the Development config and the MCP tools returned 500s until I restarted it properly. The eight log errors from that boot are the only errors in the log.
- Umbraco is still running in the background and writing to `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/umbraco-run.log`, a file I created for this session. Delete it once you stop the site.
- Nothing is committed. The project is not a git repository.
